newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine may need tiny grain imports - Kiev trade.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine may need tiny grain imports - Kiev trade.

text.p: Ukraine might consider importing small amounts of grain and soymeal to complement its poor harvest this year, but will not make big purchases because it lacks the money, agriculture industry sources said on Friday.
"There might be specific grains to import but they won't require massive imports," said a Western agricultural expert.
"They might need soymeal to improve the diet of the livestock."

The government has forecast the nearly-complete grain harvest at 26 million tonnes -- half of what Ukraine produced in 1990, but enough to cover the estimated 10 million tonnes needed for domestic needs.
Deputy Prime Minister in charge of Agriculture Mykhailo Zubets said on Thursday Ukraine would not need imports.
A Ukrainian grain official said Ukraine, which has no cash for wheat imports but barters grain with Russia, Poland and Slovakia, would not require any imports at all.
But trade and industry sources have said the harvest is of very low quality, with officials ready to blend fifth class feed grain with bread-making wheat.
One source said that if Ukraine purchased durum wheat it would be in small quantities.
"Durum won't be in big numbers," he said. "Durum is bought mostly through commercial structures and they would continue to import irrespective of the harvest."
Ukraine imported two 50,000-tonne shiploads of United States soymeal earlier this year under a PL-480 credit.
Sources said that the former Soviet republic, once the breadbasket of Eastern Europe, wanted to import last year but that record high world grain prices put a damper on plans.
"There are still sufficient supplies, and they won't import unless they need high-quality grain," said a Western trade source, adding, "this year it (the harvest) was low quality."
One trader said small quantities of soymeal and 5,000-10,000 tonnes of durum wheat had already been purchased.

Bohdan Chomiak, a representative of the Washington-based Chemonics commodities research group, said Ukraine may import some durum wheat from Canada, Australia, the United States or Argentina for local manufacture of macaroni.
The Statistics Ministry had little information on Kiev's import record but said Ukraine imported $7.1 million worth of grain from all sources over the first half of this year.
Zubets said Ukraine would export three million tonnes of mostly winter wheat from this year's harvest, most likely to Russia, Belarus and Central Asia.
"Otherwise there's enough wheat to feed everybody," said Chomiak. "There's enough bread for everybody and there will still be some left over."
